title: UIST talk dry run — TutorTrace
notes_markdown:
### Run 1 timing

- 17:40 against a 15:00 slot — cut ~3 minutes
- Slowest parts: dataset section (slides 6–9) and the related-work slide

### Talk structure (current)

1. Hook: a student stalled for 6 minutes after an error while the AI assistant sat open
2. Problem: instructors can't see which struggle is productive
3. TutorTrace: behavioral states from IDE + assistant telemetry (CS 3114 deployment, VizPI)
4. Labels: 2,340 thirty-second windows; states incl. "stalled-after-error"; kappa 0.71 across 3 raters
5. Results + the cross-course analysis promised in the rebuttal
6. Limitations: one institution, telemetry privacy, label subjectivity
7. Takeaways

### Hudson's feedback

- Cut related-work slide entirely; mention 2 papers verbally
- Slides 6–9 → merge into one "how we labeled" slide with the state diagram
- Hook is great — but say the 6 minutes slower, let it land
- Say "kappa 0.71" and immediately what that means ("substantial agreement")
- Ending is abrupt; finish on what instructors could do with it

### Likely questions (prep)

- Generalization beyond one course → cross-course analysis, still one university
- Privacy of keystroke telemetry → opt-in, no content stored for prompts beyond the session, IRB
- Why 30-second windows → piloted 10/30/60s; 30s best agreement
- Could it run live in class? → not yet; latency fine, but false positives are costly

### Logistics

- AV check with Tomás done Oct 2: HDMI + USB-C at the lectern, clicker provided (bring own anyway), timing cards at 5 / 2 / stop
- Slot: 2nd of 4 talks, 10:50–11:10; backup video (max 15:00) due on the conference portal Mon Oct 5
- Fly Mon Oct 5; talk Wed Oct 7

### Action items

- [ ] David — cut to 14:30, re-run tonight alone
- [ ] David — trim backup video to under 15:00 and upload to portal by Mon
- [ ] Hudson — text David "slow down" at 1 pm PT Wednesday (ha)
